newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary Jan-Mar soc.sec gap over 1997 target - govt.
newsitem.headline: Hungary Jan-Mar soc.sec gap over 1997 target - govt.

text.p: Hungary's January-March social security deficit overshot planned targets for the whole year but the Finance Ministry said it still planned to ensure the deficit stays within target, the ministry said on Tuesday.
"I estimate the (accumulated) deficit was between 15 and 20 billion forints in March," deputy secreatry of state Csaba Laszlo told a news conference on Tuesday.
Hungary targets a social security deficit of 13.5 billion forints for 1997.
Laszlo said the figure was only an estimate as the Finance Ministry had not yet received detailed figures for February and March from the two social security funds, covering health care and pensions.
However, the ministry said in a statement that social security contribution payments were lower than planned and added that most of the deficit was posted by the health care fund.
Laszlo said the Finance Ministry was engaged in talks with the social security funds about the possible measures by which the 1997 target could be met.
"Currently we do not consider that we should give concessions from the deficit target approve by the Parliament," he added.
The social security posted a deficit of some 73 billion forints last year, up from a target of 17.8 billion forints.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF), with which Hungary concluded a stand-by loan agreement last March, has warned the government that it should tackle the problem of soaring social security deficits.
